title: Paris protesters clash with police over living costs and public services

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the rising cost of living, declining purchasing power, and deteriorating public services.
tea.want: Demands include addressing economic hardship, inequality, government spending, and conditions in French schools.
tea.changed: Oct 19: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu called on local authorities to implement partial curfews as unrest continued.

summary: Demonstrations regarding living costs and public services escalated into widespread unrest across France, with significant clashes reported in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux, Lille, and other cities. Initiated following weeks of student protests over school conditions and teacher shortages, the movement expanded to broader economic complaints ahead of next year's presidential election. According to authorities and news reports, participants numbering in the hundreds of thousands took to the streets, where some demonstrations saw arson, looting of stores, vandalism of public buildings, and clashes with security forces. French President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, warning of legal consequences for those involved, while authorities deployed tear gas and water cannons.
demands: Address the rising cost of living
Resolve school conditions and teacher shortages
response: According to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, security forces deployed tear gas and water cannons, and approximately 1,200 people were arrested across the country. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence and vandalism, warning of prosecution.

crowd.text: approximately 550,000 people participated in the protests, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez

arrests.text: Around 1,200 people were arrested, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez

injuries.text: more than 150 police officers were injured

updates.text: Protests and clashes broke out in Paris and other French cities amid widespread demonstrations over living costs.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu called for partial curfews as unrest and clashes continued.
